extracted.intended_audience: researchers, science communicators, journalists, and public-health professionals interested in how press releases influence health news coverage
extracted.subtask_description: A PubMed search-results page aggregating research on the relationship between academic/agency press releases and health-related news coverage, focusing on exaggeration, causal claims, caveats, framing, and interventions to improve accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align headlines and main causal claims with the underlying evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Intervention tested: aligning the headlines and main causal claims with the underlying evidence (strong for experimental, cautious for correlational).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use strong causal language when the underlying evidence is experimental; use cautious, non-causal language when evidence is correlational. This alignment was evaluated as an intervention in randomized trials of press releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid causal overstatements / exaggerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Exaggerations in health news were previously found to strongly associate with similar exaggerations in press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not overstate causal relationships beyond what the study design and results support. Several observational and interventional studies emphasize reducing causal overstatements in press releases to prevent propagation into news stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include caveats and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Exaggerations and caveats in press releases and health-related science news are important determinants of how findings are represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state study limitations, uncertainty, and the appropriate scope of conclusions (e.g., generalizability, effect size uncertainty). Including caveats helps avoid simplistic or misleading headlines and coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid simplistic framing that leads to misleading claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Exaggerated or simplistic news is often blamed for adversely influencing public health; many exaggerations were already present in university press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid oversimplifying complex results into catchy but misleading claims. Maintain nuance in summaries and resist reducing findings to single declarative statements that imply causation or broad applicability when unjustified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not exaggerate explicit health advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies report that explicit health advice, when present, is sometimes exaggerated in press releases and in subsequent news articles (example: 7% of press releases and 10% of news articles exaggerated explicit health advice in one study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When offering health or behavioral recommendations, ensure advice is directly supported by the evidence and avoid overstating the magnitude, certainty, or applicability of recommended actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame press releases carefully during public-health emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of press releases and news coverage (e.g., 2009 H1N1 influenza pandemic) maps how framing devices develop from agency press releases to news stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During pandemics or other public-health crises, pay particular attention to framing (risk emphasis, protective actions, uncertainty) to avoid miscommunication or undue alarm; trace and monitor how framing may be transformed in news coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve accuracy of academic press releases to improve news accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Improving the accuracy of academic press releases is proposed as a mechanism to improve the accuracy of subsequent news coverage, though some studies found no clear increase in uptake from more accurate releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize factual accuracy and fidelity to the study findings in academic press releases. While greater accuracy may not always increase media uptake, it reduces the chance that exaggerations will propagate into news reports.
